K14 on Windows: profile show --file refuses, with exit 2 USAGE_ERROR in 17-46 ms, each of: a directory (plain, trailing backslash, \\?\), NUL/nul, dir\NUL, \\.\NUL, \\?\NUL, CON, CONIN$, CONOUT$, \\.\CON, an empty path, the NPFS root \\.\pipe\, a missing pipe, a junction to a directory, a FileShare.None-locked file, a byte-range-locked file, a pipe served by another process that accepts and never writes (\\.\pipe\ and \\.\PIPE\ forms), an outbound-only pipe and a busy pipe (ERROR_PIPE_BUSY returns at once).
The GetFileType(FILE_TYPE_DISK) check does not reject legitimate profile files. These all return PROFILE_OK: a \\?\ path, an alternate data stream, a ::$DATA path and a relative path.

agent list --socket refuses every non-pipe path I tried with exit 5 AGENT_UNAVAILABLE, before writing anything. Content sha256, size, mtime and attributes stayed unchanged for a regular file (with é in the path), an empty file, a read-only file, a hidden file, the \\?\ form, a relative form, ::$DATA, an existing ADS (its content also unchanged), a file held FileShare.Read by another handle, a directory (plain and trailing backslash), a junction, NUL, CONOUT$, CONIN$, \\.\pipe\ and an empty path. A non-existent path and a non-existent ADS were not created (stream count unchanged).

agent list on pipes served by a separate PowerShell process of the same user: byte-mode and message-mode answers and the \\?\pipe\ prefix give AGENT_OK. The server saw exactly 00000001 0b and no extra bytes. A type-5 reply gives AGENT_REFUSED (exit 5). Accept-and-close, an outbound-only pipe and accept-and-never-write (1022 ms with --timeout-ms 1000) all give AGENT_UNAVAILABLE (exit 5).

§9.6 batch ruling, argument bytes: Rust std's escaping delivered every metacharacter argument exactly to the child, with no injection. This covered & | " \" ^ ( ) @ ! %VAR% %VAR:~0% %VAR:b=c% %cd% %=C:% %~dp0 %% and unterminated %, and a % spanning two arguments, through a full path, FWD.BAT in upper case, a trailing-space path, a \\?\ path and a bare-name PATH lookup. Overriding the CD variable or defining a variable named 'cd:~,' does not break the %%cd:~,% hack. CR and LF arguments are refused (exit 127, InvalidInput). ::$DATA and verbatim literal trailing-dot/space batch names are refused with exit 127. A bare name resolved only through PATHEXT (fwd → fwd.bat) is not found (127). A decoy cmd.exe in the working directory, first on PATH or in ComSpec was never used.
The fix's comments hold on the host: opening a named pipe never waits, a busy pipe fails at once, and opening a regular file read/write without writing changes neither content nor mtime.

refuted_claims.claim: REPORT.md §16: 'Rust passed all four run.batch_target.* rows already, because std refuses .bat/.cmd arguments it cannot escape (the CVE-2024-24576 fix)'.
refuted_claims.evidence: In my ps51 run, all 16 cases of each of the 4 run.batch_target rows have outcome received_exactly; none were refused. Std escapes the arguments (quoting plus the %%cd:~,% hack) and refuses only CR/LF (and NUL). My probes batch.arg.newline and batch.arg.cr gave exit 127 InvalidInput; every other shape was received exactly. The outcome is right but the stated mechanism is wrong.

defects.description: Not a regression and not code this round changed (pre-existing std behaviour, outside the fix's diff). Needs an orchestrator ruling on scope: §9.6 says 'no argument byte' and does not say whether argv[0], the script path, is covered. When the batch file's own path contains %NAME%, Rust std puts the script path into the cmd.exe /e:ON /v:OFF /d /c ""<script>" args" line without the %-escaping it applies to the arguments, so cmd.exe expands it. Observed: (a) an env var whose value holds '" & break>file & "' plus a directory named pct%HMRDIRVAR%x led to a second command running (file created, outcome INJECTED); (b) <dir>\os%OS%y\fwd.bat ran a different batch file, <dir>\osWindows_NTy\fwd.bat, with exit 0, while the intended one never ran. Control: a direct CreateProcessW of the same .bat path through .NET Process.Start without heimdall-proto also runs the other file, so the root cause is cmd.exe; std just does not mitigate it for the script path. Either way it is an M01 input for the product's batch-launch policy: refuse a % in a batch path, or escape it.
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/runner.rs (Windows launch through std::process::Command; std make_bat_command_line); evidence: tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-r4/x1b/review-rust/probe/results.jsonl cases batch.scriptpath.*, batch2.*

defects.description: Pre-existing std behaviour, not a §9.6 violation (no injection), recorded for M01 resolution policy. For a batch path with a trailing dot or trailing dots and spaces (fwd.bat., fwd.cmd., 'fwd.bat. . .'), std detects the batch file through GetFullPathNameW but passes the un-normalized name to cmd.exe. cmd then reports '"...\fwd.bat." is not recognized' and run exits 1 (CHILD_EXITED, launched) instead of running the file or refusing with 127. A trailing space ('fwd.bat ') works.

defects.description: Documentation inaccuracy: REPORT.md attributes the passing run.batch_target.* rows to std refusing arguments it cannot escape. In fact std escapes them and the child receives them exactly; it refuses only CR/LF/NUL. See refuted_claims.

Recorded, not gating. On Windows, opening a pipe path given as profile show/tui --file connects to the pipe server before GetFileType rejects it. A separate-process StallPipe server logged 2 connects for my 2 successful opens. No bytes are read or written, and the result is USAGE_ERROR in about 18 ms as §9.6 requires. But §5 says tui makes no 'agent contact', and --file \\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent would make one connection to a real agent. A path-prefix pre-check cannot cover every pipe alias. M01 should decide whether a connection without traffic counts as contact.

summary:
The fix round's claims hold, and I found no regression. My clean rebuild reproduces all four artifacts byte for byte. The unchanged X1 script, run natively against my build, gives rust gating 71/71 on both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, with all 94 verdicts identical to the fix round. The 2.4.2 harness passes 139/139 on darwin-arm64 and on linux-arm64 (container).

The two GetFileType checks (profile: must be FILE_TYPE_DISK; agent: must be FILE_TYPE_PIPE, checked before the write) fail closed and are confined to #[cfg(windows)]. I probed 129 cases beyond the script: devices, \\?\ and ::$DATA forms, ADS, junctions, locks, and busy, outbound-only and never-writing pipes served by other processes of the same user. None of the profile/--file, --socket or agent-pipe probes failed, and no non-endpoint path was modified or created.

For batch files, std escapes every argument shape I tried, so no argument injection occurred. Two pre-existing std/cmd.exe issues outside the round's diff remain:
- **%NAME% in the batch script path** (argv[0]) is expanded by cmd.exe. That allowed env-driven command injection and ran a different .bat file. A direct CreateProcessW shows the same, so cmd.exe is the root cause. This needs an orchestrator ruling on whether §9.6 covers argv[0].
- **Trailing-dot batch names** fail in cmd.exe with exit 1 instead of running or being refused with 127.

Also recorded: REPORT.md misstates why the batch rows pass, and opening a pipe given as --file connects to its server without traffic, which matters for §5 tui's 'no agent contact' (M01 input).

Status: verified (evidence preserved, real exit codes). Evidence is in <repo>/tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-r4/x1b/review-rust/: build/, harness/, windows/review-ps51-a and review-ps7-a, probe/results.jsonl and probe/tools/, tools/, staged-root.sha256 and commands.txt. Host and Mac scratch were removed; no processes were left running.
